digest.component_or_area: IAM policy and Bedrock service integration
propositions: The review-bot container must obtain Bedrock credentials authorized for the Converse API through the existing instance role, not through long-term bearer tokens or a separate credential broker.

The Converse API authorization check is `bedrock:InvokeModel`, not the distinct `bedrock:Converse` action, as proven only by real runtime calls from the scoped role—policy simulators answer what the policy permits for a named action, not which action the service actually checks.

IMDS is reachable from the review-bot container (confirmed by successful IMDSv2 token PUT and role resolution), so the solution is IAM-only and does not require raising `http_put_response_hop_limit` from its default value.

The scoped inline policy must grant `bedrock:InvokeModel` and `bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream` on Claude foundation models and cross-region inference profiles with wildcarded regions, residing in a new `infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf` to preserve the single-owner contract in `iam.tf` (lines 4–9).

Verification requires three layers: policy simulation (necessary but insufficient), a real Converse call from the instance as the scoped role (the only proof of which action the service checks), and a negative control (a non-Claude model returning AccessDeniedException to prove scope binding).

The verification recipe and from-instance test protocol must be recorded in `infra/runbooks/` so future operators can re-verify the grant without repeating the error-prone simulator-only approach or over-trusting calls made under wildcard-holding identities.
